mechanism: AC-CRC (Adversary-Calibrated Conformal Risk Control / Dual-Channel Convex E-Gate)

formulation.jointConvexEValue: E_M^joint(tau) = w_1 * E_M^det(tau) + w_2 * E_M^adv(tau), w_1 + w_2 = 1
formulation.theoreticalScopeNote: Convex e-value averaging E_joint = w1*E_det + w2*E_adv preserves E[E_joint] <= 1 and anytime Ville error control P(sup_t E_t^joint >= 1/delta) <= delta under arbitrary inter-channel dependence for the intersection/safety-monitoring null (and composite risk w1*R_det + w2*R_adv). For offline simultaneous union-null certification, active channels additionally enforce non-losing channel drift E_i >= 1 alongside E_joint >= 1/delta.

analyticalCheck.proofSummary: For any w1, w2 >= 0 with w1 + w2 = 1 and any joint law P in H_0 (arbitrary correlation rho in [-1, 1]) satisfying E_P[E_t^det] <= 1 and E_P[E_t^adv] <= 1, E_P[w1*E_t^det + w2*E_t^adv] = w1*E_P[E_t^det] + w2*E_P[E_t^adv] <= w1 + w2 = 1; non-negative supermartingale closure implies P(sup_{t>=1} E_t^joint >= 1/delta) <= delta by Ville's maximal inequality.

honestAssessment.summary: Across 3 document-cluster splits, AC-CRC w=(0.5, 0.5) shifts held-out released top-1 re-identification rate by -1.32 pp and E2E detector leak rate by +0.84 pp vs single-channel HC-CRC, with a safe-yield delta of +0.00 pp. Dependent-channel Monte Carlo (10000 trials across 5 copula correlations) confirms E[E_joint] <= 1 and anytime exceedance <= delta=0.05. Operational caveat: computing C_adv(x) requires auxiliary K-candidate dossier scoring via a local LLM attacker, making AC-CRC best suited to offline batch release audits or high-risk escalations rather than sub-millisecond inline WASM streaming.
